samples.summary:
Crash-vs-gate-failure disambiguation is done by grepping a prose sentence in the workflow, rather than by fixing the ambiguous contract at its source (mark-ready.mjs).

The root problem is that mark-ready.mjs uses exit 1 for both "a gate said no" (mark-ready.mjs:184) and node's own crash code. The fix chosen here lives entirely in the consumer: the YAML hard-codes the literal "Not promoting: one or more gates are not satisfied" and greps the log for it. The producer already owns its exit-code space (0/1/2/3 with 3 free-standing codes and 4+ unused) and the repo's established pattern for cross-file string contracts is an exported marker constant (`HANDOFF_MARKER` in scripts/agent/disclosure.mjs, imported by mark-ready.mjs:39). Either a dedicated exit code for "gates unsatisfied" or a marker line would keep the contract machine-readable and single-sourced; a human-readable report sentence duplicated into YAML is now load-bearing and can only be kept honest by the cross-file test added in this diff. Cost stays inside the codebase (the test does guard it), so minor.

The canonical harness design doc's "Ready gate" bullet documents the three gates but not the promote job's exit-code contract, and this change makes that contract materially more elaborate (four enumerated codes + `*)` default + a verdict-line corroboration for exit 1, with a cross-file string dependency). Nothing in docs/design records that a bare exit 1 is no longer trusted, so the next editor of mark-ready.mjs's report text has only the test to warn them. No behavioral cost, so minor/low.

The consumer-contract test has grown from four regexes into a small parser of the workflow YAML (window bounded by the next `- name:`, a `case` block matcher, a branch map, a quote-blanking `exits()` helper). That is a lot of shell-parsing machinery living in a node:test file to assert workflow behavior; a shell-level check (e.g. driving the block with stubbed statuses) or a much smaller invariant would fit the layer better. Taste/level-of-abstraction only.

Two of the added tests (the `name === "CI"` filter test and the GH_MUTATION_TOKEN routing test, plus the new GH_STUB_TOKEN_LOG plumbing) cover pre-existing behavior in mark-ready.mjs unrelated to the exit-code/consumer-contract change this diff is about. Additional coverage is not harmful, but it is scope beyond the change and makes the diff harder to read as one intent.
